Topic1.Title: Opening, Announcements, and Declarations
Topic1.Summary: The meeting opened with an announcement about the Better Public Meetings Project, inviting community members to rate their meeting experience via a scorecard. The Council held roll call and a moment of mourning for Lafayette council member Tony Briggs. Declarations were presented for Hispanic Heritage Month and Energy Efficiency Day.

Topic2.Title: Open Comment Period
Topic2.Summary: Eight in-person speakers and one virtual speaker addressed the Council on topics including library building disposition, Black history exhibit invitations, homelessness and public safety near Central Park, child-friendly restroom facilities, a Landmarks Design Review Committee demolition, and a Boulder Junction housing project. Staff responded to several comments, including praise for the child-friendly cities initiative and acknowledgment of the incident near the Band Shell.

Topic3.Title: Consent Agenda and Call-Up Check-In
Topic3.Summary: The Council unanimously approved consent agenda items 3A through 3F. For call-up check-in item 4A, a site review for a two-story Life Sciences facility at Walnut Street, no Council member requested to call it up. Council praised the project as an exemplary sustainability model.

Topic4.Title: Boulder Junction Phase 2 (TVAP) Amendments
Topic4.Summary: Staff presented amendments to the Transit Village Area Plan for Boulder Junction Phase 2, introducing new land use categories (mutod, mui, pkuo), place types, urban design updates, and revised transportation connections. The Planning Board recommended approval with one revision regarding office uses that staff did not support. Council discussed market conditions, anti-displacement strategies, and future implementation steps before unanimously approving both motions.

Topic5.Title: Affordable and Modest-Size Housing Zoning Ordinance (85-99)
Topic5.Summary: Staff presented Ordinance 8599 to amend land use code provisions on site review, density, parking, and subdivision standards to encourage affordable and modest-size housing. Planning Board and Housing Advisory Board largely supported the changes with some reservations about single-family zone density. Council debated several amendments, including efficiency unit use review and far increases, and ultimately passed the amended ordinance unanimously on second reading with further items deferred to a future phase.

Topic6.Title: Letter to County Commissioners on Proposed Housing Tax
Topic6.Summary: Council Member Benjamin proposed a letter endorsing a county ballot measure for an affordable and attainable housing tax, requesting investment in permanent supportive housing and transitional housing. Council agreed to send the letter with revisions, and staff clarified that a formal resolution of support would come later. The item was scheduled for consent on October 5.
